questions.q: Roughly how many people diagnosed with ADHD may not have it?
a: About one in six
About one in twenty
About one in three
About one in fifty
questions.why: Lesson 1 says up to 1.1 million of 6.4 million diagnoses may be wrong.

questions.q: Why is ADHD so often misdiagnosed, according to the summary?
a: The criteria are outdated and observers make the call
Testing equipment is too costly for most clinics
Symptoms only appear in adulthood
Parents exaggerate their children's behavior
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes a short checklist, observed children and few specialists.

questions.q: What does the summary say about ADHD medication?
a: It is overprescribed and can bring serious side effects
It is the safest option for most children
It works best when started in adulthood
It has no effect on growth or appetite
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns about addiction and effects on growth and weight.

questions.q: How can exercise help children with ADHD?
a: It sharpens focus and plays to their strengths in team sports
It tires them out so they sit still in class
It removes the need for structure at home
It mainly helps them sleep through the night
questions.why: Lesson 3 says activity before class aids focus and suits their shifting attention.

questions.q: What advantage does the summary link to ADHD?
a: Lateral thinking that produces creative connections
A stronger memory for details and routines
Greater patience with repetitive tasks
A natural ability to follow strict schedules
questions.why: Lesson 3 points to inventive solutions and unusual combinations as strengths.
